context:
The test is an integration test that stitches together existing components.
No new production code should be needed unless show-plan/compare-plans lack
a callable Python API (w1). Use DuckDB for zero external dependencies.
The test verifies the full serialization round-trip, which is the gap the
current unit tests do not cover.
description:
No test currently exercises the full plan capture pipeline end-to-end:
  benchbox run --capture-plans
  → result bundle (results.json / run_metadata.json with plan_fingerprints)
  → benchbox show-plan <results-dir> <query-id>
  → benchbox compare-plans <run1> <run2>

Unit tests cover individual adapters (test_postgresql_plan_capture.py,
test_duckdb_plan_capture.py) and live integration tests cover the adapter
against a real database. But none verify:
  - That --capture-plans correctly propagates plan data into the result bundle
  - That plan_fingerprints appear in run_metadata.json with the correct format
  - That benchbox show-plan can read and display a captured plan from a bundle
  - That benchbox compare-plans correctly identifies changed vs unchanged plans

A regression in any intermediate serialization step (result dict → JSON
→ ResultManifest → CLI display) would go undetected by the current test suite.

The test should use DuckDB (no external credentials, in-memory database) with
a small trivial workload (SELECT 1, SELECT 2+2) so it runs in unit/fast CI
without service containers. The test is an integration test: it invokes the
run orchestrator via its Python API (not subprocess) and inspects the output.

Test shape:
  1. Run a minimal DuckDB benchmark with capture_plans=True
  2. Assert run_metadata.json contains plan_fingerprints for each query_id
  3. Assert each fingerprint is a 64-char hex string (SHA256)
  4. Run the same benchmark again and assert fingerprints are identical (stability)
  5. Invoke show-plan programmatically and assert it returns a non-empty plan
  6. Invoke compare-plans on the two runs and assert "unchanged" for all queries

The show-plan and compare-plans steps (5 and 6) test the round-trip through the
CLI layer. If those commands do not exist as testable Python entrypoints, add
thin wrappers or test through the underlying functions directly.

anti_patterns.dont: add the E2E test to the live_postgresql or postgres-integration jobs
anti_patterns.why: DuckDB in-memory is the test platform.

anti_patterns.dont: invoke benchbox run as a subprocess
anti_patterns.why: use the Python API to avoid subprocess marshaling complexity and make the test debuggable.

anti_patterns.dont: use real TPC-H data in the E2E test
anti_patterns.why: SELECT 1 and SELECT 1+1 are sufficient to exercise plan capture; real data takes minutes.

preserves.behavior: Existing adapter-level plan capture unit tests must remain untouched.
The E2E test must complete in under 30 seconds (fast marker; DuckDB SELECT 1 is sub-millisecond).
The E2E test must not require network access or external credentials — DuckDB in-memory only.

work_units.notes:
Locate benchbox/cli/commands/ for show-plan and compare-plans commands.
If they exist as Click commands, extract the underlying Python functions
so they can be called from tests without invoking a subprocess.
If they don't exist as stable Python callables, add thin wrappers in
benchbox/core/query_plans/ that the CLI commands delegate to.
The goal: show_plan_for_run(results_dir, query_id) → str
           compare_runs(run1_dir, run2_dir) → ComparisonReport
work_units.summary: Identify or create programmatic entrypoints for show-plan and compare-plans

work_units.notes:
Location: tests/integration/test_plan_capture_e2e.py or
tests/integration/platforms/test_plan_capture_e2e.py.
Mark with: pytest.mark.integration, pytest.mark.fast (DuckDB in-memory).
Use tmp_path fixture for the results directory.
Step 1: Create DuckDBAdapter with capture_plans=True, run SELECT 1 and
        SELECT 1+1 as a minimal two-query benchmark.
Step 2-3: Assert run_metadata.json (or equivalent) contains
          plan_fingerprints with 64-char hex strings.
Step 4: Run the same two queries again with a fresh adapter, compare
        fingerprints from run 1 and run 2 — must be identical.
Step 5: Call show_plan_for_run() and assert non-empty string output.
Step 6: Call compare_runs() and assert no plan changes detected.

The test is marked integration + fast, so it should run under the existing
integration job in pr.yml (which already runs integration tests). Verify it
is collected by:
  uv run -- python -m pytest tests/integration/ -m "integration and fast" --collect-only -q
If not collected, check pytest.ini addopts and markers.
